Irre- coverable losses in the form of evaporation from open water surfaces and transpiration by noncrop vegetation were estimated to be 5 per cent of the difference between supply and total consumptive use. The total nonconsumptive use less the 5 percent difference between supply and total consumptive use was assumed to represent ground-water replenishment in the form of infiltration. Recharge by loss from the Kings River and minor streams was added to estimates of infiltration to obtain total recharge. The discharge elements of the ground-water equation comprises net ground-water outflow, irrigation pumpage, and consumptive use of ground water on urban and suburban lands within the area. Finally, the change in the ground-water storage was obtained as the difference between recharge and discharge. The estimates of recharge and discharge elements for the years 1948 and 1952 are summarized in tables 22 and 23.
